props.description:
Before you perform an Accuracy Check, a Magic Check for an offensive spell, or a Check to advance or turn back a Clock, you may declare:

💬"double or nothing"

If you do and the Check triggers a critical success, double the damage dealt by that attack or spell, or the filled/erased sections of that Clock, respectively; however, any other kind of success becomes a failure instead.
props.name: Double or Nothing

props.description: After an enemy you can see performs an action during a conflict, you may declare one of your deck’s suits (after the action has been resolved) and put the top card of your deck into your discard pile, face up. If that card is a joker or its suit matches the one you declared, you may immediately perform the Spell action for free, casting a spell with a total Mind Point cost equal to or lower than [SL × 5] (you must still pay its MP cost).

You gain a deck, a hand and a discard pile (see Unique Mechanic).

During a conflict, you may use an action and spend up to [10 + (SL × 5)] Mind Points (minimum 10). If you do, resolve 1 card from your hand for every 5 MP spent this way (to a maximum of 5 cards; these cards form a set). After you resolve the effect of the set (if any), discard these cards and draw that many cards from your deck.

During a conflict, if you have two or fewer vanguard cards in play, you may use an action to choose 1 card from your hand and place it face down as a vanguard card; if you do, draw 1 card from your deck.

At the end of each conflict, if you have one or more vanguard cards in play, shuffle them back into your deck.

props.classMechanic_text:
ACE OF CARDS — MANAGING THE DECK

Shuffle, draw, make a set, and unleash a flashy effect. That’s the whole trick! This page explains the Magic Cards mechanic used by the Ace of Cards, written like a video game tutorial and faithful to the book, with a few beginner tips sprinkled in.

1) What you need

  • A 30-card deck: 2 jokers + 28 cards split into 4 suits, each suit containing the values 1–7 (so 7 cards per suit).
  • Suits = damage types: when you create your character, assign each suit to a damage type: Air, Earth, Fire, Ice.
  • Using a poker deck? Remove face cards and the 8–10s; you’ll be left with A(=1)–7 in each suit. Tarot minor arcana or CCG cards also work if the values/suits are easy to read.

2) When a conflict starts

  1. Shuffle all 30 cards into a face-down deck.
  2. Draw your starting hand of 5 cards.

Hand & Discard: Cards you draw go to your hand (only you see them, but you may show them if you want). When you discard from your hand, place cards face up into your discard pile in any order—once placed, the order in the discard pile cannot be changed.

Out of cards? If you need to draw but the deck is empty: draw as many as you can, then shuffle the discard into a new deck (face down) and keep drawing.

End of conflict: deck, hand, and discard only exist during conflicts. When a conflict ends, shuffle all 30 cards back together and set them aside.

3) The core move: resolve a set

Many Ace of Cards abilities ask you to resolve a set. A set is a specific pattern of cards from your hand that you place on the table to trigger an effect.

  • Match exactly. If an effect asks for “exactly 4 cards,” then 5 cards won’t work—even if they also contain the pattern.
  • Jokers are wild. When your set includes jokers, you choose the joker’s suit and value (1–7) as you play the set.
  • If a set qualifies for more than one effect, choose only one to apply.
  • “Consecutive values” means sequences like 1-2-3-4 or 4-5-6-7 (no wrap-around).

4) Set Recipes & Effects (Cheat Sheet)

Level bonus: Blinding Flush, Double Trouble, and Magic Flush deal +10 damage if you are level 20+, or +20 damage if you are level 40+.

EffectExact Set RequiredWhat it does
Jackpot4 cards of the same value (no jokers)You and all allies recover 777 HP and 777 MP. Any PCs who Surrendered but are still on the scene immediately regain consciousness (their Surrender’s other effects remain).
Magic Flush4 consecutive values of the same suitDeal damage to all enemies equal to 25 + the total values of the cards. The damage type = the suit’s assigned type (Air, Earth, Fire, Ice). (+10 at Lv20+, +20 at Lv40+)
Blinding Flush4 consecutive values (any suits)Deal damage to all enemies equal to 15 + the total values of the cards. The damage type is Light if the highest value in the set is even, or Dark if it’s odd. (+10 at Lv20+, +20 at Lv40+)
Full Status3 of a kind + a pair

Choose two among: Dazed, Shaken, Slow, Weak.
If the highest value in the set is even → you and all allies recover from those statuses.
If it’s odd → each enemy suffers those statuses.

Triple Support3 of a kindYou and all allies regain HP and MP equal to (sum of values) × 3.
Double TroubleTwo pairsDeal damage equal to 10 + the highest value in the set to up to two different enemies you can see. The damage type is your choice among the suits present in the set. (+10 at Lv20+, +20 at Lv40+)
Magic PairOne pairMake a free attack with a weapon you have equipped. If it deals damage, choose a suit among the set’s suits: the attack’s damage becomes that suit’s type (e.g., becomes Fire if you chose the Fire-assigned suit).

5) Quick examples

  • Magic Flush: 3♣-4♣-5♣-6♣ → values sum = 18 → damage to all enemies = 25 + 18 = 43, type = the suit’s assigned type (if ♣ = Air, then it’s Air).
  • Blinding Flush: 1♥-2♣-3♦-4♠ → sum = 10, highest value = 4 (even) → damage to all enemies = 15 + 10 = 25, type = Light.
  • Full Status: 3♦-3♣-3♥ + 5♠-5♦ → highest = 5 (odd) → each enemy suffers two chosen statuses (e.g., Slow and Weak).
  • Joker use: For 1-2-3-Joker (any suits) as a Blinding Flush, set the Joker to “4” to complete the straight.
  • Jackpot reminder: Needs four of a kind with no jokers (e.g., 6♣-6♦-6♥-6♠). Jokers cannot appear in this set.

6) Beginner tips

  • Think in patterns. Keep an eye on four-of-a-kind, three-plus-two, two pairs, a single pair, and runs (1-2-3-4 etc.). Most hands naturally lean toward one of these.
  • Jokers save sets. Because you set their value and suit, they complete straights and pairs easily. Don’t waste them on Jackpot—Jackpot forbids jokers.
  • Use even/odd on purpose. For Blinding Flush and Full Status, the highest value’s parity steers the outcome (Light vs Dark, cleanse allies vs debuff enemies). Choose the top card wisely.
  • Know when to go wide vs precise. Magic Flush and Blinding Flush hit all enemies; Double Trouble snipes two targets but lets you pick the damage type from the suits you used.
  • Reset rhythm. Don’t fear running out of deck—the discard will reshuffle back in. Cycling is part of the plan.

7) Ultra-fast reference

  • Start: Shuffle 30 → draw 5.
  • Play: When an ability tells you to “resolve a set,” put down the exact pattern, apply one matching effect.
  • Jokers: Wild; choose suit & 1–7. (But no jokers allowed in Jackpot.)
  • Discard: Face-up; order can’t be changed after placing.
  • Deck empty: Shuffle discard into new deck and keep going.
  • End of conflict: Shuffle all 30 together and put away.

8) Suit–Type reminder (fill this for your character)

  • ♣ = Air
  • ♦ = Earth
  • ♥ = Fire
  • ♠ = Ice

(You can assign them differently—pick once when you create the character and stick to it.)

That’s it!

Shuffle up, fish for the set you need, and choose the effect that best fits the moment. If your hand looks awkward, remember: jokers bend fate, and the discard will come back around.

props.class_lore:
Aces of Cards make use of special decks to perceive the constant fluctuations of the stream of souls. Each deck is inextricably connected to its user and reflects their taste and personality: by drawing specific combinations at the right moment, an Ace of Cards manipulates magical energy to produce supernatural effects.

In some worlds, Aces of Cards duel against each other using their personal decks, in a quest for glory or in order to obtain precious artifacts.
